concepts.title: Emergence of Macroeconomics
concepts.definition: Macroeconomics as a separate branch emerged out of the Great Depression that began in 1929; microeconomic reasoning could not explain the collapse of output and employment, and John Maynard Keynes' General Theory (1936) built the analysis of economy-wide aggregates.
concepts.key_idea: The Depression was the empirical puzzle that forced economists to study inflation, unemployment and national output as aggregates.

concepts.title: Unemployment During the Great Depression
concepts.definition: In the USA, from 1929 to 1933, the unemployment rate rose from 3 per cent to 25 per cent as workers were thrown out of jobs, illustrating how an economy-wide collapse differs from a market-level disequilibrium.
concepts.key_idea: The rise in the unemployment rate is the difference between the peak rate in 1933 and the trough rate in 1929.

solution_steps.explain: trough rate 3 per cent in 1929, peak rate 25 per cent in 1933
the difference gives the percentage-point rise

concepts.title: Stocks, Flows and Capital
concepts.definition: Macroeconomics distinguishes stocks (quantities measured at a point of time, like the capital stock or wealth) from flows (quantities measured over a period, like income or investment); capital is a produced means of production that adds to the stock.
concepts.key_idea: Classifying a variable as stock or flow decides which accounting identity it can enter, and mixing them produces measurement errors.

solution_steps.explain: capital stock and wealth are point-of-time magnitudes; income and investment accrue over periods

capital adds to the stock only through the flow of investment net of depreciation

concepts.title: Circular Flow of Income
concepts.definition: In the simplest two-sector economy, households supply factors of production to firms and receive factor incomes; firms sell goods and services back to households, so the income of one sector is the expenditure of the other and the circular flow closes.
concepts.key_idea: The circular flow identity - what is spent by firms is the income of households and what households spend is the revenue of firms - underlies all national income accounting.

solution_steps.explain: factors flow from households to firms and goods flow back as money returns to households

worked_examples.question_pattern: Classify capital, investment, wealth and income as stock or flow, with a one-line justification each.

solution_template.explain: capital and wealth are measured at a point of time

worked_examples.question_pattern: Explain the circular flow between households and firms in three steps.

solution_template.explain: households supply land, labour, capital and enterprise to firms
firms pay wages, rent, interest and profit back to households
households spend their income on the goods firms produce, closing the circle
